# barduck

> Lightweight self-hosted personal dashboard for collecting values from
> shell commands, scripts, and HTTP push, storing historical data in
> embedded DuckDB, and exposing it through a web UI, TUI, CLI, and JSON API.

barduck is a Rust single-binary dashboard designed for personal and
home-server data. It is useful when Grafana or a full observability stack
(Prometheus + Grafana and similar) is more than a small personal dashboard
needs.

## Core capabilities

- Collect values from shell commands run on a schedule (`query` sources)
- Collect values from long-running commands emitting JSON lines (`stream` sources)
- Receive values pushed over HTTP (`ingest` sources, `/api/ingest`)
- Composite sources: one command reporting several independently-tracked values
- Store historical data in embedded DuckDB (one file, plain SQL)
- Define sources and dashboard layouts in TOML
- Web UI (live-updating)
- Terminal UI (TUI, ratatui)
- CLI (`latest`, `logs`, `fetch`, `poll`, `tui`)
- JSON API and JSON output for all CLI commands
- Single binary deployment
- Nix / home-manager integration (systemd user service)

## Good use cases

- Personal home dashboards
- Home server dashboards
- Self-hosted infrastructure dashboards
- Monitoring scripts, commands, and small APIs (via shell commands)
- Tracking personal metrics (bank balance, work hours, domain expiry, etc.)
- Receiving webhook/event data over HTTP push
- Lightweight alternative to Grafana for personal use
- Local dashboards backed by DuckDB, queryable with plain SQL

## Not a good fit for

- Large-scale production observability
- Distributed metrics collection
- Prometheus-compatible scraping
- Enterprise RBAC or multi-tenant dashboards

## Technology

- Rust
- DuckDB (embedded)
- TOML
- Ratatui (TUI)
- HTTP / JSON API
